root.label: Constant Expressions
root.note: Compile-time evaluation obeys strict abstract-machine rules governed by constexpr, consteval, and constinit.

children.label: Core Constant Rules
children.note: Core constant expressions disallow runtime-only operations, dangling outputs, and all undefined behavior.

children.label: No undefined behavior
children.note: Signed overflow, out-of-bounds reads, and inactive union access fail to compile.

children.label: No dangling results
children.note: Final constant values cannot point to local stack slots or unfreed heap storage.

children.label: Manifestly constant contexts
children.note: static_assert, template arguments, constexpr vars, and consteval calls force compile-time evaluation.

children.label: Three Specifiers
children.note: Each keyword controls timing and mutability differently across variables and functions.

children.label: constexpr allows compile time
children.note: constexpr functions run at compile time or runtime; constexpr variables are implicitly const.

children.label: consteval forces compile time
children.note: Immediate functions execute solely during translation and reject runtime arguments.

children.label: constinit enforces static init
children.note: constinit prevents dynamic initialization order bugs while keeping static or thread-local variables mutable.

children.label: Transient Allocation
children.note: C++20 allows dynamic allocations inside constant evaluation provided they are freed before returning.

children.label: Compile-time new and delete
children.note: Dynamic allocations and deallocations succeed inside constexpr evaluation contexts.

children.label: Allocations cannot escape
children.note: Heap pointers from constant evaluation cannot persist into runtime global objects.

children.label: Copy to std::array
children.note: Extract results from temporary std::vector buffers into fixed arrays to persist data.

children.label: Dual-Path Branching
children.note: Select portable compile-time logic or optimized runtime code within one constexpr function.

children.label: std::is_constant_evaluated
children.note: Returns true inside a plain if statement only during constant evaluation.

children.label: if constexpr trap
children.note: Wrapping std::is_constant_evaluated inside if constexpr always evaluates to true.

children.label: C++23 if consteval
children.note: Enters an immediate context that avoids the trap and permits calling consteval helpers.

children.label: Subtle Boundaries
children.note: Specifier placement and function pointers follow rules distinct from ordinary runtime code.

children.label: Pointer top-level const
children.note: constexpr on a pointer variable makes the pointer itself const rather than the pointee.

children.label: Immediate function pointers
children.note: Taking the runtime address of a consteval function is ill-formed outside constant evaluation.
